Responsive UX · Wireframe study

City of Phoenix

I recreated the City of Phoenix homepage at two screen sizes to see how it helps people find services amid city announcements, news, and resources.

Design focus Use wireframes to discuss which services should be easiest to find across screen sizes.

Explore the designs ↓

OverviewDesign decisionsReflection & next steps

PROJECT CONTEXT

Project and approach

Someone who needs to report a problem is looking for something different from someone browsing local news. I recreated the homepage in low fidelity so I could compare how those tasks are grouped and what appears first on desktop and mobile.

01 / DESIGN DECISIONS

Find the shortcuts residents rely on

On desktop, I looked at how the page groups tasks like paying a bill, reporting an issue, and finding trash pickup information. Those shortcuts sit alongside heat relief information, city news, and government resources. Redrawing the layout made it easier to see which tasks have a direct entry point.

02 / DESIGN DECISIONS

Compare what comes first on mobile

I compared a 1440 px desktop layout with a 390 px mobile layout. On a narrow screen, more of the content has to stack vertically, so the order of the sections plays a bigger role in what people find before they scroll.

REFLECTION

What I learned and what I’d test next

The two layouts make it easier to compare what residents see first at each width. If I took this into a redesign, I’d test a few common mobile tasks, such as reporting a problem or finding heat relief, and watch where people look first. That would give the team a basis for deciding which shortcuts should move up.
